A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLEG by the same authors, with identifiable correspondence between methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable Appendices A–I.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and segmentation experiments on ScanNet, comparisons with per-scene methods, and ScanNet++ ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark comparisons and ablations, plus semantic-sparsity, camera-pose, depth-estimation, and unseen-Replica results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, novel-view selection, instance contrastive learning, and isotropic semantic-Gaussian aggregation remain substantially the same; DGLE largely renames the earlier sparsification strategy. V2 explicitly adds LPIPS to the photometric objective and changes photometric/feature weights from 1/1 to 2/0.5. Appendix A newly documents depth consistency and supervision of both Gaussian representations, without establishing when these procedures were introduced.

E1.justification: V1 trains using InstanceMV-14K, assembled from ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes, and RealEstate10K. V2 reports training only on ScanNet and ScanNet++. Appendices D–F add explicit camera-pose and depth-estimation tasks and evaluation on unseen Replica scenes. ScanNet++ itself is retained coverage, already used for v1 ablations.

E2.justification: V2 adds AnySplat and SAM2+CLIP to the main comparisons and VGGT to the new pose/depth comparisons. LSeg, LSM, Uni3R, LangSplat, and LangScene-X remain evaluated, but LSeg/LSM/Uni3R no longer have 32-view comparison rows. These changes substantially broaden and revise the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Fixed-view baseline evaluation changes from DUSt3R-style post-processing to selecting the two input views nearest each target. The training image pool changes from N=14 to N=12, and mask preparation changes from projected scan annotations to the described SAM2 pipeline. V2 revises view sweeps, drops runtime measurements, and introduces pose AUC and depth AbsRel/threshold-accuracy protocols.

E4.justification: V2 Table 3 expands the original distillation, contrastive-loss, and sparsification ablations with separate voxel/pixel embedding controls and an isolated novel-view-distillation ablation. Appendix C adds semantic voxel-size sensitivity and its storage–accuracy tradeoff. Appendix F explicitly tests cross-dataset generalization on unseen Replica, substantially extending robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 Table 3 averages across input-view settings; this does not introduce repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Benchmark values and result coverage are substantially revised. For example, ScanNet two-view FLEG mIoU/PSNR changes from 47.12/24.20 to 48.01/25.05 under the revised training/evaluation regime, not an established same-setting gain. V2 Table 3 reports 73.89K embeddings and 18.04 MB versus 2.012M and 491.3 MB for its pixel variant. Tables 4–6 add pose, depth, and Replica results; v1's runtime results are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical training objective is revised through the additional LPIPS term in Equation 4 and independently weighted loss terms in Equation 12. The projection, contrastive complexity, moment-matching, and isotropic-covariance derivations remain essentially unchanged. Neither version introduces a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: V2 withdraws InstanceMV-14K construction as a central contribution and reorganizes the contribution around dual-branch distillation and compact semantic representation. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion add the concrete claim of comparable semantic fidelity using fewer than 5% of pixel-aligned embeddings and emphasize preventing input-view overfitting. Arbitrary-view reconstruction and multitask capabilities remain core claims.

C2.justification: V2 develops the interpretation that novel-view distillation mitigates input-view overfitting and qualifies semantic sparsity with observed degradation at excessive sparsity. Appendix I newly identifies dependence on VGGT geometry, generalization demonstrated primarily indoors, and memory difficulties with hundreds or thousands of images. These materially qualify applicability beyond v1's discussion.

D1.justification: V2 discloses eight H200 GPUs and approximately two training days, additional loss details, validation/frame sampling, pose alignment, float32 storage accounting, and a default semantic voxel size. Appendix A adds previously undocumented supervision details. Conversely, v1's AdamW, cosine schedule, peak learning rate, and backbone multiplier disappear. Reproducibility remains imperfect: Appendix C states a default voxel size of 0.016, while Figure 5 labels it 0.16.

R1.justification: The same broad research areas remain, with targeted additions including DF-3DGS's semantic sparsity, several pose-free/self-supervised reconstruction methods, and a formal IGGT citation. V2 removes the EA3D discussion and revises its distinction from IGGT. These refine prior-work positioning without replacing the overall literature framework.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around compact semantics. Method sections are reorganized into dual-branch distillation and a dedicated DGLE section, replacing the earlier dataset-centered exposition. Appendices A–I introduce a substantial new document structure.

P2.justification: V2 changes to a single-column layout, redraws the teaser and pipeline, and reorganizes qualitative comparisons by reconstruction versus segmentation. Tables 1–3 gain new structures, dataset groupings, metrics, and highlighting. New Tables 4–6 and Figures 5–13 display geometry evaluations, sparsity sensitivity, generalization, and additional scene visualizations.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central method: Table 3 better isolates compactness and novel-view supervision, while Appendices C–F test sparsity limits, geometry, and unseen-scene generalization. Explicit limitations also make applicability easier to assess. These address important evidential gaps in v1. The gains outweigh lost optimizer/runtime information and reporting defects, including Figure 5's inconsistent voxel-size labels and Table 2's malformed SSIM entry. This assessment rests on stronger controls and clearer boundaries, not the revised performance values alone.
